solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rabbit on cake for breakfast

definitions.meaning: to rabbit on is British slang for talking at tedious length without saying much
a crisp battered griddle cake with a grid pattern, eaten at breakfast

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the verb for rambling talk and the gridded batter cake served at breakfast.

clue.text: Plant exists in water, I suspect

indicators.note: in places the verb piece inside the rearranged letters
suspect as an adjective means dubious or not genuine, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
exists means is, as in 'there is'

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a plant is growing in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like a verb in the surface but works as an adjective, meaning dodgy, signalling the anagram of WATER plus I, which gives WTERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing shrub with hanging lilac flower clusters, so a kind of plant.

clue.text: Struggle as a swimmer

definitions.meaning: to struggle clumsily, as in mud or water
a flatfish, so something that swims

explanation.definitionFit: The verb for floundering about and the name of a flatfish share one spelling.

clue.text: Supporter downed emissary

parts.note: a leg supports a table or a body
downed food means ate it

explanation.surface: A fan knocks down a visiting diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downed' suggests knocked over, but here it means swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal envoy or diplomatic representative, so an emissary sent on a mission.

clue.text: Star and tiger after a mauling

indicators.note: a mauling tears something apart, so the letters are torn up and reordered

explanation.surface: A celebrity is mauled by a tiger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a mauling' rearranges AND TIGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, cool, late-stage star with a reddish glow is a type of star.

clue.text: Skirt adopted by landed gentry

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A skirt is taken up by the landed gentry.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across landED GEntry.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt something is to go round its border, which is what edging along does.

clue.text: Underdog's out — though shouldn't be out?

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: An underdog is dismissed, though wrongly given out.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'out' signals the anagram of UNDERDOG; the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grounded child is confined to the house as a punishment, so must stay in.

clue.text: Seven characters are so sweet

parts.note: the seven letters T to Z are the ones that come ... in the alphabet

explanation.surface: Seven people are so lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'are so' as 'come after S': only T, U, V, W, X, Y and Z do, seven characters. AFTERS is British slang for a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for the pudding or dessert course served after the main meal.

clue.text: "Heart" label, not "head"

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a sticker is an adhesive label

explanation.surface: A tag that says 'heart' rather than 'head'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not "head"' drops the first letter, S, of STICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the heart, which keeps ticking like a clock.

clue.text: Shed in Berkshire town

definitions.meaning: to cast off skin, as a snake does
a large town west of London in the county of Berkshire

explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning to cast off dead skin and the name of a Berkshire town share a spelling.

clue.text: Sceptic acting so indecisively

indicators.note: indecisively suggests wavering this way and that, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doubter behaves without conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that God's existence cannot be known is a religious sceptic.

clue.text: Sixtieth one of thirteen?

definitions.meaning: the gemstone marking a sixtieth anniversary or jubilee
a card of the red suit with thirteen cards in a pack

explanation.definitionFit: The gem of the sixtieth jubilee and any card of the thirteen-card suit share one name.

clue.text: German figure set off, not out to become genius

parts.note: the German number one is ein

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a batsman not out is still in

explanation.surface: A German statue is set off on its way to becoming a work of genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET into STE.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist's surname is used as a byword for a brilliant mind.

clue.text: Plant on middle of French dish

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it
the central letters of the word are taken

parts.note: a tree is a plant

explanation.surface: A vegetable sits in the middle of a French meal.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' means coming after, so the plant follows the French letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish served as a course, the main course in America or before it in Britain.

clue.text: Pig maintaining messy home, one way or another

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

indicators.note: messy means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pig keeps its home in a mess, one way or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maintaining' reads as keeping up a house in the surface, but it means holding, with 'messy' as the anagram signal for the home.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning by some means or other, unclear how.

clue.text: Numbers needing no introduction for US composer

indicators.note: the introduction is the first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: fives are numbers

explanation.surface: Musical numbers that need no introduction for an American composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' drops F from FIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer.

clue.text: Permit male prisoner to enter always

indicators.note: the pieces go into the other word

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
POW stands for prisoner of war

explanation.surface: Allowing a male prisoner to come in at any time.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER is the poetic contraction of 'ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower is to give authority to, which is to permit or license.

clue.text: Underwear left among explosives, might you say?

indicators.note: among puts the letter inside the other word

parts.note: a playful coinage, boomers as things that go boom

explanation.surface: Underwear left lying among bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might you say?' admits that BOOMERS for explosives is a made-up word.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned loose knickers gathered at the knee, so underwear.

clue.text: Time for some hot stuff?

definitions.meaning: British slang for a prison sentence, as in doing time
a hot breakfast dish of oats cooked in milk or water

explanation.walkthrough: Doing PORRIDGE is British slang for serving time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The oat breakfast is eaten hot, and the same word is slang for a jail term.

clue.text: Perfect fraud, primarily, criminal

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: lawless means criminal

explanation.surface: A perfect fraud, mostly criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a single flaw means perfect.

clue.text: General risk to keep thin

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a bet is a risk
lank means thin and lean

explanation.surface: An army general takes a gamble to stay slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' poses as an officer, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanket as an adjective means covering all cases, so general or across-the-board.

clue.text: Money brought over for organ

indicators.note: brought over means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: loot is slang for money

explanation.surface: Cash is brought over to pay for a church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the male sex organ.

clue.text: A certain flow

parts.note: bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: A steady, sure flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to be plentiful, flowing in large numbers.

clue.text: Joining a similar partner, is able to dance

indicators.note: the piece is joined by another just like it, so it appears twice

parts.note: can means is able

explanation.surface: Someone paired with a matching partner is able to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively high-kicking French music-hall dance.

clue.text: Heater storing drink for cold course

indicators.note: storing holds one piece within another

parts.note: the sun heats the Earth
kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: A heater holding a drink for a chilly lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heater' looks like a household appliance; here it is the sun, which heats the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowy slope for skiing down is a course in the cold.

clue.text: Light with which artist captures energy

indicators.note: to capture is to enclose, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Francis Bacon was an Irish-born British painter
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An artist captures the energy of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captures' puts E inside BACON.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal fire or lighthouse lamp guiding ships is a light.

clue.text: Dawn, bird after man

indicators.note: after places the bird piece behind the man piece

parts.note: cock is an old form of address, man to man
a crow is a bird

explanation.surface: At dawn, a bird pursues a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The time the rooster calls, at daybreak.

clue.text: Taken by Arab, a Kurdish capital

indicators.note: taken by means held within, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A Kurdish capital captured by an Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across araB A KUrdish.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Azerbaijan, on the Caspian Sea.

clue.text: America flexing muscle, and endlessly

indicators.note: flexing bends things, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: America showing off its strength without limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts AND to AN; 'flexing' rearranges MUSCLE plus AN.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in stars and stripes personifies the United States.

clue.text: Something of a nose for a game

definitions.meaning: the bony upper ridge of the nose
a card game played by four in partnerships

explanation.definitionFit: The upper part of the nose and the trick-taking card game share one name.

clue.text: Beast long gone is around, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An extinct beast is surprisingly still around.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct prehistoric reptile is a beast that died out long ago.

clue.text: Political philosopher sticks by purpose, almost entirely

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an end is a purpose or aim
gels means sticks together or sets

explanation.surface: A thinker sticks closely to his purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' removes the last letter, D, from the word for purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels co-wrote the Communist Manifesto, a political philosopher.
